title: NY State Assembly · District 64
area: Staten Island's East Shore and part of southern Brooklyn (Bay Ridge), including St. George, Tompkinsville, Grasmere and Grymes Hill.

context.text: Both parties' primaries were canceled. Incumbent Michael Tannousis advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party primaries unopposed; Shpetim Qorraj advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.

summary.text: Michael Tannousis is the Republican and Conservative incumbent Assembly Member for District 64, first elected in 2020. A lawyer and former Bronx and Richmond County assistant district attorney who began in public service as an aide to City Council Minority Leader James Oddo, he describes his priorities as protecting crime victims, changing recent bail and judicial-discretion reforms, and affordability.

background.text: Tannousis describes himself as a lifelong Staten Islander and the son of Greek immigrants who came to the U.S. after being displaced by armed conflict in Cyprus.
He graduated from Public School 23, Intermediate School 24 and Monsignor Farrell High School, earned an undergraduate degree from SUNY Binghamton, and received a J.D. from Pace Law School.

He began his public-service career in 2006 as an aide to then-Minority Leader James Oddo of the New York City Council; his Assembly biography also lists service as Counsel to City Council Member Joseph Borelli.

After law school he became an Assistant District Attorney in the Bronx DA's office in 2011, then joined the Richmond County DA's office in 2016 under DA Michael McMahon, where he prosecuted violent-crime and narcotics cases.
He was elected to the Assembly on November 3, 2020, defeating Democrat Brandon Patterson for the seat previously held by Nicole Malliotakis; he took office January 1, 2021.
He was re-elected in 2022 and 2024 and is the Republican and Conservative nominee in 2026. His district covers parts of Southern Brooklyn and the East Shore of Staten Island.
Assigned in 2025-2026 to the Cities, Codes, Governmental Employees and Judiciary committees.

He previously served as a board member of the Cyprus-US Chamber of Commerce and as a delegate for the Cyprus Federation of America, and lives in the Great Kills neighborhood with his wife, according to his Assembly biography.

priorities.text: Stand up for Republican and Conservative values in Albany.
Roll back criminal-justice policies from Albany that he opposes, including bail reform.
Improve quality of life in Staten Island and Brooklyn.
Bring his prosecutorial experience to Albany to support law enforcement.
Create conditions for small businesses to thrive.

positions.summary: Sponsored legislation to repeal congestion pricing in Manhattan.

record.text: Prime-sponsored A06680, which would repeal congestion pricing, restructure MTA board appointments to include one member per NYC borough, and require an independent forensic audit of the MTA; held for consideration in the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee 17-8 on May 28, 2025.
Prime-sponsored A09346 (with Pirozzolo as a co-sponsor), which would incorporate a separate City of Staten Island with its own charter; referred to the Cities Committee.

Prime-sponsored A06358, which would restore judicial discretion in bail decisions and require risk-and-needs assessments for felony defendants; as a member of the Codes Committee, voted no on the committee's 16-6 vote to hold his own bill for consideration (rather than advance it) on May 13, 2025.

Prime-sponsored A06996, which would prohibit siting and construction of battery energy storage systems in Assembly District 64; held for consideration in the Local Governments Committee 14-6 on May 18, 2026.

candidates.name: Shpetim Qorraj

summary.text: Shpetim Qorraj, who goes by Tim, is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Michael Tannousis. According to his campaign website, he was born in Kosovo, came to the United States in 2011, owns a Staten Island services business and has led nonprofit organizations serving immigrant families. His campaign priorities include affordability, transportation, healthcare, public safety, education and East Shore flood protection.

background.text: According to his campaign website, Qorraj was born in Kosovo and lost his father, a veteran, at age 13 during the war there; he came to the United States in 2011 and now lives in the South Beach neighborhood of Staten Island.
He says he holds a Master's degree in Criminal Law.
He owns Skyler Services Group LLC, a Staten Island business providing renovation, porter, super and maintenance services.
His campaign website says he has led the formation of nonprofit organizations that support immigrant families and gives a voice to the Albanian community and other Staten Islanders.
He describes himself as a father of two sons in Staten Island public schools and an active PTA member, living with his wife and children.
He is the 2026 Democratic nominee, also on the Affordable & Safe Party line, after the June 23 Democratic primary was canceled.

priorities.text: Address New York's affordability crisis, including housing costs, small-business regulatory burdens, and the cost of utilities, food and other essentials.

Secure state funding for Staten Island transportation, including keeping the Verrazzano Bridge resident toll discount, reducing congestion on Hylan Blvd, and creating a fast-ferry dock in Great Kills.
Support public education funding and after-school programming, and push for construction of the East Shore seawall promised after Hurricane Sandy.

positions.summary: Calls for hiring more police officers for the 122nd Precinct and for the state to enhance retirement benefits for first responders to attract recruits.
positions.quote: Support increasing hiring of police officers to be assigned to the 122 Precinct and expand the Community Affairs department to have more officers on call to address quality of life issues.

candidates.researchNotes: No completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or independent news coverage was found for Qorraj, but his campaign website (linked from his Ballotpedia infobox) has an about page and issues page that were used for background and priorities.

statements.quote: We need real solutions to expand affordable housing options and protect tenants.
statements.context: On his campaign website, in the affordability section
